figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: The PREFILL band shows a single 'token + position' box for a pass the caption calls 'the one-shot parallel pass over the whole prompt', inviting the reading that prefill processes one token at a time — the exact misconception the prefill/decode distinction exists to prevent.
evidence: PREFILL band: 'prompt -> token + position -> transformer -> logits + sampling -> first token' (one box). DECODE band: 'previous token -> token + position -> transformer -> logits + sampling -> next token' (one box, correctly, since decode is one token per step). Caption: 'PREFILL (top) is the one-shot parallel pass over the whole prompt.' The two bands are visually identical in token granularity, so the parallelism of prefill is carried only by prose.
root_cause: The bands were drawn with a shared template that does not encode the one distinguishing property of prefill.
correction: Label the prefill box 'tokens + positions (all in parallel)' and the decode box 'token + position (one per step)', and/or draw the prefill box as a stack/fan of tokens with a 'parallel' annotation. Consider adding a small 'N tokens at once' vs '1 token per step' cue.
acceptance_test: A reader who sees only the figure (no caption) can state that prefill processes all prompt tokens in one parallel pass while decode processes one token per step.

figure: FIGURE 2.1 — The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline
issue: Layout inconsistencies: the italic note 'conceptual per-step, per-layer cache I/O' sits inside the DECODE band against its top border; the band labels are placed inconsistently ('PREFILL' above its band, 'DECODE' inside its band); the 'read' and 'append' arrows are only ~0.35 in apart with their labels offset to opposite sides, which is tight for a figure whose whole point is the read/write distinction.
evidence: Rendered positions: 'PREFILL' at x~90-140, y~125-135 (above the band frame); 'DECODE' at x~165-200, y~335-345 (inside the band frame); the italic note at x~355-460, y~330-345 (inside the band, touching its top rule); 'read' label left of a downward arrow at x~285 and 'append' label right of an upward arrow at x~310.
root_cause: Bands were drawn and labelled iteratively without a final alignment pass.
correction: Place both band labels in the same position relative to their frames (e.g. above-left of each frame), move the italic note into clear space below the DECODE band or into the caption, and separate the read/append arrows (e.g. route 'read' down the left of the cache box and 'append' up the right) so each label sits directly above its own arrow.
acceptance_test: Both band labels occupy identical relative positions; no annotation touches a frame rule; each of 'read' and 'append' sits directly above the arrow it names.

issue: The drawn roofline is inconsistent with its labeled ridge (~295) and peak (1e15 FLOP/s): the black memory-bound segment starts at ~1e12 FLOP/s at AI=1 and reaches 1e15 at ~295, which implies bandwidth ~1e12 B/s and ridge ~1000, not ~295. The decode marker at AI~1, ~3e12 FLOP/s therefore sits above the drawn roof.
evidence: Axes: x 'arithmetic intensity (FLOP/byte)' 1..10000; y 'attainable performance (FLOP/s)' 1e11..1e15. Black line starts at (1,1e12), corner at red dashed 'roofline ridge ~295' and flat roof 1e15. Caption: 'decode at ~1 FLOP/byte' and '~295 ridge'. Roofline formula: attainable = min(peak, B*AI); B = peak/ridge = 1e15/295 ≈ 3.39e12 B/s, so at AI=1 the roof is ~3.39e12, not 1e12. The red decode dot is plotted at ~3e12, above the drawn line.
acceptance_test: Recompute B from the stated peak and ridge; redraw the memory-bound segment through (1, B) and (ridge, peak) with slope 1 on log-log axes; place the decode marker on or below the roof (or replace it with a non-quantitative regime label); verify no marker lies above the roof and that the ridge label matches the drawn corner.

figure: Figure 2.2 — caption, italic 'Two distinct conclusions' note, item (1) Regime
issue: The caption places the canonical prefill point at '~0.2K FLOP/byte, well to the right of the ~295 ridge.' 0.2K = 200 FLOP/byte, which is LEFT of the 295 ridge, so the printed number contradicts (a) the figure itself — the blue 'prefill' marker is drawn at ~10^4 (≈9K), not at 200 — and (b) the same sentence's 'well to the right of the ridge' clause. The correct first-order prefill intensity is ≈ L ≈ 9.2K FLOP/byte (each weight is read once while doing ~L FLOPs per weight), which is what the figure shows.
evidence: Recompute: prefill FLOPs ≈ 2·P·L = 2·70e9·9200 ≈ 1.29e15; weight bytes ≈ 140e9; intensity ≈ 1.29e15 / 1.4e11 ≈ 9.2e3 ≈ 9K. The figure's x-axis puts the prefill triangle at ~10^4. The ridge 295 = 989e12 / 3.35e12 (peak/bandwidth), so 200 < 295 ⇒ memory-bound side, directly contradicting the 'compute-bound regime' the same note asserts. The non-italic caption ('long-prompt prefill lands at high intensity — the compute-bound side') is correct; only the italic number is wrong.
acceptance_test: Change '~0.2K FLOP/byte' to '~9K FLOP/byte (≈ the 9.2K input length)'. Re-read the sentence: the number must now lie to the right of the 295 ridge and agree with the figure's marker position.

figure: Figure 2.2 — caption, italic note, item (2) Capacity
issue: The caption states the single-H100 theoretical peak as '0.980 PFLOPS'. The canonical FP16 dense peak is 989 TFLOPS = 0.989 PFLOPS; 0.980 is not a rounding of 989 and is inconsistent with the figure's own ridge arithmetic and with the book's H100 convention.
evidence: 989 TFLOPS = 0.989 PFLOPS. The figure's ridge (295 FLOP/byte) × 3.35e12 B/s ≈ 9.88e14 ≈ 0.989 PFLOPS, i.e. the plot is drawn for 0.989, not 0.980. The 1.19 PFLOPS demand in the same note is correct (1.29e15 FLOPs / 1.08 s prefill budget ≈ 1.19e15), so only the peak figure is off.
acceptance_test: Replace '0.980 PFLOPS' with '0.989 PFLOPS (989 TFLOPS)'; confirm the demand-vs-peak margin is unchanged and the value now matches the figure's ridge (295 = 989/3.35).

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The caption's stated prefill arithmetic intensity (~41 FLOP/byte) contradicts BOTH the plotted marker (~10^4 FLOP/byte) and the prose on the same page (~2K FLOP/byte). Three mutually inconsistent values are given for the single quantity the figure exists to convey. Worse, the caption's own number (41) is BELOW the ridge the figure labels (~295), so taken at face value the caption places prefill on the memory-bound side while simultaneously calling it 'the compute-bound side'.
evidence: Caption (printed p.23): 'Low-batch decode (streaming weights per token) lands at ~1 FLOP/byte — the memory-bound side; long-prefix prefill lands at ~41 FLOP/byte — the compute-bound side.' Prose list item (1) on the same page: 'arithmetic intensity places the canonical prefill point ~2K FLOP/byte, well to the right of the ~295 ridge'. Figure: the blue 'prefill' triangle sits at the far right of the x-axis, at or beyond the 10000 tick (AI ~ 1e4), not at 41 and not at 2e3. Independent rederivation for the canonical 70B / 9,200-token prefill: FLOPs = 2 x 70e9 x 9200 = 1.29e15; bytes = 140 GB weights + 2.62 MB/token x 9200 = 24.1 GB KV writes = 1.64e11 B; AI = 1.29e15 / 1.64e11 ~ 7.8e3 FLOP/byte (plus ~17% from attention FLOPs -> ~9e3). None of 41, 2e3, or 1e4 is derivable from the canonical numbers as printed; 41 is also implausible on its face, since prefill AI is approximately the number of tokens processed (AI ~ T for large T), so 'long-prefix prefill' cannot be 41.
root_cause: The figure, its caption, and the summary list were authored from three different (unstated) derivations of the same quantity; no single derivation is shown anywhere on the page, so no gate could catch the divergence.
correction: Pick one canonical prefill AI, show its derivation (tokens, FLOPs, bytes, ratio) in the caption or in an adjacent worked example, and make the caption, the marker position, and the prose list item all state that same value. If the intended value is the derived ~8e3, move the marker to ~8e3 and rewrite the caption as '~8x10^3 FLOP/byte — the compute-bound side'. If a different scenario (e.g. a short prompt) is intended, label it as such and plot a second marker rather than silently changing the number.
acceptance_test: One number appears for canonical prefill AI in the caption, in the marker x-position, and in prose item (1); the value exceeds 295 (so 'compute-bound side' is true of the stated number); and a reader can reproduce it from the canonical inputs printed in Ch. 4 / Table 2-1 without consulting another chapter.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The drawn roofline ridge is geometrically inconsistent with its own '~295' crossover label and with the H100 numbers the book uses elsewhere, and the decode marker is drawn ON the ridge, contradicting the figure's own annotation that markers lie below the roof.
evidence: A roofline's bandwidth-limited segment is a straight line in log-log with slope = HBM bandwidth and NO intercept; it must pass through (AI=1, performance = bandwidth). For H100 SXM (FP16 dense 989 TFLOPS, HBM3 3.35 TB/s) the ridge is performance = 3.35e12 x AI, i.e. it crosses the 989 TFLOPS peak at AI = 295 and passes through (1, 3.35e12). The drawn line instead intercepts the y-axis at ~1e12 at AI = 1 and reaches 1e15 at AI ~ 295; those two constraints cannot be satisfied by one straight line (the drawn line implies a bandwidth of ~1.6 TB/s and a crossover at ~600, or, if the drawn slope is 1 decade/decade, a bandwidth of 1 TB/s and a crossover at 1000). The red 'decode' circle at (1, ~1.2e12) is drawn directly on the black ridge line, while the in-figure annotation states 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'. The decode marker should sit clearly BELOW the ridge (roofline at AI=1 is 3.35e12; decode at batch 1 achieves ~3.35e12 only in the idealized bandwidth-bound limit, and real kernels sit below it).
root_cause: The ridge was drawn by eye against the axis limits rather than computed from the peak/bandwidth pair, so the intercept, the crossover label, and the marker placement were never reconciled.
correction: Redraw the ridge from the actual numbers: bandwidth-limited segment through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 9.89e14), with the compute-bound plateau at 9.89e14 (label it 989 TFLOPS, not 1e15). Place the decode marker at (1, ~1e12) clearly below the ridge, and the prefill marker at its derived AI and at a plausible sub-peak performance (e.g. 3-5e14). If the intent was to show decode sitting exactly on the bandwidth roofline, say so in the caption and remove the 'run below the roof' annotation.
acceptance_test: The drawn ridge satisfies performance = 3.35e12 x AI for AI <= 295 and performance = 9.89e14 for AI >= 295; the '~295' label coincides with the drawn crossover; no marker lies on the ridge line unless the caption explicitly says it is on the roofline; the y-axis plateau is labelled 989 TFLOPS.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode on the roofline ridge
issue: The figure states no hardware, precision, or peak/bandwidth basis, so the ridge label '~295' and the y-axis ceiling '1e15' are uninterpretable in isolation; the surrounding prose then treats the 1e15 axis top as 'the regime peak' for an H100 whose FP16 dense peak is 989 TFLOPS.
evidence: Figure contains only 'roofline ridge ~295' and a y-axis labelled 'attainable performance (FLOPS)' with a 1e15 top tick. Prose item (3) on the same page: 'The regime peak (1.0x10^15 FLOPS) — so one H100 is insufficient under that analytical deadline model.' 989 TFLOPS = 9.89e14, not 1.0e15; the axis ceiling is a plotting choice, not a hardware peak, and the caption does not say so.
root_cause: The figure was designed as a conceptual schematic but is read (and cited in the prose) as a quantitative H100 roofline.
correction: Add a subtitle inside the plot: 'H100 SXM, FP16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 -> ridge at 295 FLOP/byte'. Label the plateau '989 TFLOPS (FP16 dense)' rather than leaving 1e15 as an unlabeled ceiling, and either drop the '1.0x10^15' phrasing in prose item (3) or state that 1e15 is the axis limit.
acceptance_test: A reader who has never seen the book can state, from the figure alone, which GPU and precision the ridge represents and why the crossover is at 295.

issue: In the conclusions list beneath the figure, the capacity item's unit reads as '~1.19 FLOPS/FLOP demand', which is not a unit; the intended quantity is presumably ~1.19x10^15 FLOP/s. If the exponent is genuinely absent, the comparison to the 989 TFLOPS H100 peak does not parse.

figure: FIGURE 3.1 — panel B, masked discrete diffusion
issue: In the masked-diffusion lane the sequence GROWS from three tokens to four across the corruption step, which implies that masking changes sequence length. For a book whose later chapters reason about per-token KV growth and context-length arithmetic, a figure that shows length changing under corruption is a substantive mis-teaching.
evidence: Panel B: left state shows three cells 'A | cat | sat'; the corrupted state shows four cells 'A | M | sat | M'; the fully masked state shows four cells 'M | M | M | M'. The left box is also visibly narrower than the other two. A corruption process q must preserve length; the caption calls the panel 'a categorical-MASK lane' and notes 'text states are illustrative token IDs, not generated results'.
acceptance_test: Make all three states the same length (e.g. 'A | cat | sat | sat' → 'A | M | sat | M' → 'M | M | M | M', or 'A | cat | sat' → 'A | M | sat' → 'M | M | M') and keep the three boxes the same width; re-check that the 'M = MASK' note still explains every cell.

issue: Panel A labels its three states; panel B does not, so the reader must map the three boxes by position alone and infer which is clean, which is corrupted, and which is fully masked.
evidence: Panel A carries 'clean diffusion data', 'partly corrupted', 'noise prior' beneath the three boxes. Panel B's three boxes have no labels; the only key is the note 'M = MASK; text states are illustrative token IDs, not generated results.'
acceptance_test: Add the same three state labels under panel B's boxes, or restructure the figure with one shared label row serving both lanes, so the two lanes are read identically.

issue: The 'noise prior' state is drawn as a structured histogram rather than an uninformative one, so the visual contrast between structured data and isotropic noise is absent and the reader can infer that the prior retains the data's structure.
evidence: Panel A, right box labelled 'noise prior', shows bars of clearly unequal heights (a tall bar at the left, shorter bars elsewhere) whose profile closely resembles the 'clean diffusion data' panel. The caption calls the drawing 'Conceptual drawing, not a measurement', which does not license a structurally misleading profile.
acceptance_test: Draw the noise-prior panel with a flat or near-uniform bar profile (or annotate it '≈ uniform / uninformative') so the contrast with the structured clean-data panel is unambiguous; retain the 'not a measurement' caveat.

figure: FIGURE 3.2 — Dependency order and cache lifetime, panel B
issue: The caption claims out-of-order acceptance, but the diagram shows strictly in-order, left-to-right acceptance. The distinction between 'full-canvas masked sampler' and 'block-causal sampler' is exactly the point of the figure, and the drawing does not exhibit it.
evidence: Caption: 'a full-canvas masked sampler: accepts positions out of order while recomputing bidirectional states'. Panel B draws: fixed prompt → [? ? ? ?] → [A B C ?] → [A B C D]. Every accepted ID appears in its final left-to-right position, and the dashed recompute region always covers the rightmost unresolved cells. acceptance_test: Either redraw panel B so at least one accepted ID appears out of position (e.g. [? B ? ?] → [A B C D], with the dashed recompute region covering the whole canvas), or amend the caption to 'accepts selected IDs while recomputing bidirectional states' and add a note that the drawing shows one in-order acceptance order for illustration. issue: The figure's legend vocabulary refers to a 'solid bracket' element that the drawing does not contain, and the one mark that could play that role appears in only one panel. A reader cannot tell which visual element encodes 'finalized prefix state'.
evidence: Note under panel A: 'Solid brackets mark finalized prefix state, not just accepted IDs.' Caption: 'Solid brackets identify finalized prefix state'. The drawing contains only per-cell boxes (all solid) plus dashed orange recompute rectangles; no bracket element distinguishes finalized from non-finalized state, and the trailing '-' cell in panel A's last group is drawn identically to the finalized 'A B C' cells. A short underline appears beneath the trailing cell of panel A's third group only, and is explained nowhere. figure: FIGURE 3.3 — Wan2.2 A14B: active ≠ resident parameters
issue: The horizontal connector between the two stage boxes is drawn as a plain data-flow arrow and can be read as the high-noise stage's output feeding the low-noise stage, rather than as temporal progression of the denoising schedule. Its label also duplicates the arrowhead with a trailing '→' glyph.
evidence: A solid horizontal arrow runs from the 'High-noise stage' box into the 'Low-noise stage' box, with the text 'Denoising schedule progresses →' centred above it. The temporal meaning is carried only by the label and by the figure's note 'Not two experts within one forward' and the caption's 'as the denoising schedule progresses'; the connector itself has the same visual grammar as the data-flow arrows elsewhere in the book.

figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue: The MoE resident-memory components shown in the figure do not visibly sum to the stated total. The figure labels 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)' and 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)' and then states 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB'. The two visible components sum to about 91 GB; the missing ~3 GB is the always-on/shared resident weight, which is mentioned only in the per-token active-compute line ('1.4B always-on') and in the caption's italic paragraph, not as a resident-memory component.
evidence: Figure 3.4 labels: 'inactive experts ≈ 68 GB (6 × 11.4)'; 'active experts ≈ 23 GB resident (2 × 11.4)'; 'MoE total resident ≈ 94 GB'. Arithmetic: 68.4 + 22.8 = 91.2 GB. The caption and italic paragraph identify 'always-on attention/shared weights (~1.4B)', which at FP16 is ~2.8 GB, giving ~94.0 GB total. The figure does not label that resident component, so the displayed decomposition does not close.
acceptance_test: Add an explicit always-on/shared resident component to the MoE legend (e.g. 'always-on/shared ≈ 3 GB') or restate the total as '≈ 91 GB experts + ≈ 3 GB always-on = ≈ 94 GB'. Recompute the displayed components so that they visibly sum to the stated total within rounding.
